html:
SMTO-CTR-0026 — SMTO's safety check of the task plan couldn't finish

GUID: c5a09c4a-65f3-44a5-84f3-81dc2d2701ac
Slug: task-contract-integrity-unavailable
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: ctr

What happened

  • Before starting work, SMTO checks the plan it wrote from your request for risky additions. That check broke before it finished, so SMTO didn't act on this version of your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Retry on the task, or open the Task contract step under the task and select Retry contract generation. Retry writes the plan again and runs the safety check again from the start.
  2. If it fails the same way again, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. A safety check that keeps breaking points to a fault inside SMTO, not a problem with your request.
  3. Leave Task Contract Integrity Guard switched on in the composer's Options menu. That guard blocks plans that add file or folder locations, or saved @ values, that your request didn't include; turning it off removes that protection.

What success looks like

  • The Task contract step shows Task contract generated and the task starts working.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details, with the time it happened, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the task, and don't turn off the Integrity Guard; the saved attempt is needed to find the fault.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Task Contract Integrity Guard raised an internal error before producing a pass/fail result, so the compiler failed the attempt closed (integrity_guard_internal_error) and authorized no actions for this revision.

What this means

  • The enabled local integrity verifier raises an exception before producing its pass/fail authority result, and the compiler returns a non-retryable guard-internal failure. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • The enabled local integrity verifier raises an exception before producing its pass/fail authority result, and the compiler returns a non-retryable guard-internal failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the integrity_guard_internal_error occurrence separately from a proven authority violation.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server log for the exception raised inside check_contract_integrity during _run_compiler_attempt, and the attempt's integrity_validation findings in the Task contract activity. Retry generation once with the task's Retry control; if it recurs, report it as a defect with the log excerpt. Do not disable the Integrity Guard or delete the attempt record to work around it.
  • Inspect the Task Contract activity diagnostics and retry generation through its existing controls. Preserve the Integrity Guard; report a repeated verifier failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The verifier defect is resolved and the enabled guard completes for an intended supported new attempt.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
